field_changes.before:
The ordered display/runtime levels are off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max and ultra. A nonreasoning model always reports only off; a reasoning model filters this ordered list using its thinkingLevelMap.

A map value null removes a level. xhigh/max/ultra are included only when their map value is defined and non-null; ordinary levels remain available when omitted. clampThinkingLevel returns an already supported request, then searches upward from its index, then downward; an unknown value or no remaining level falls back to the first available or off. The source test with xhigh:null, max:'max' requires xhigh to clamp to max, not high. A mapped ultra value survives the helper and is forwarded by compatible OpenAI requests (ice:packages/ai/src/models.ts:900-941; ice:packages/ai/test/max-thinking.test.ts:35-85; ice:packages/ai/test/max-thinking.test.ts:105-121).

Budget-based adapters use clampReasoning, which maps xhigh/max/ultra to high. Default budgets are minimal1024, low2048, medium8192, high16384; caller budgets override per level. With no explicit caller cap the model ceiling contains thinking; with a caller cap, thinking is added but capped by model/hard authority. If the ceiling does not exceed the thinking budget, thinking shrinks to leave 1024 ordinary output tokens. AI-006 owns hard-authority validation. modelsAreEqual compares only provider and id, returning false if either model is absent; metadata updates do not create a new identity.

field_changes.before:
Rust implements nearly the whole transform in the Anthropic request module, including signature removal, omission placeholders, pending-call repair and skipped failed assistants (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/anthropic/build_params.rs:223-478). Its helper hardcodes Anthropic ID normalization rather than accepting a provider callback; synthetic result timestamps are0 rather than current time. It trims the signature when deciding presence, unlike TS truthiness, and can turn a foreign empty thinking block with a nonblank signature into empty text instead of dropping it; later Anthropic serialization normally filters that text. Its scalar-value ID replacement emits one underscore for an astral character where the TS non-Unicode regex emits two. Typed deserialization rejects null content instead of admitting it to this helper; that boundary difference is deliberate and should be documented. Other native adapters have separate projection logic and require their own review.

Native `String` already excludes lone surrogate code points. Anthropic therefore implements its named sanitizer as a pass-through, while the image adapter's scalar filter cannot encounter a surrogate in a valid `&str`; these are representation differences, not a missing native text-cleaning feature (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/anthropic/build_params.rs:704-709; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/images.rs:426-433).

field_changes.before:
The direct stream accepts AnthropicOptions, while streamSimple authenticates synchronously and builds the shared base envelope before selecting adaptive or budget-based thinking. Request assembly precedes onPayload, the hard max is enforced again afterward, SDK retries are disabled, and the shared HTTP retry wrapper obtains the raw response before awaiting onResponse and publishing start.

Direct options add thinkingEnabled, thinkingBudgetTokens, effort including ultra, thinkingDisplay=summarized|omitted, interleavedThinking, toolChoice=auto|any|none|{type:tool, name}, and a prebuilt client. Injecting a client skips client construction/auth checks and fixes the OAuth transform flag to false. Default direct thinking is omitted; streamSimple without reasoning explicitly sets thinkingEnabled=false. forceAdaptiveThinking=true selects adaptive mode, with the model's thinkingLevelMap string winning over low/medium/high fallback. Otherwise it fits the configured/default thinking budget inside model/context/hard limits while reserving ordinary output. The expression at line 847 was connector-redacted and is not reconstructed. Direct budget zero is falsy and becomes1024 in buildParams, a source edge case that must not be described as preserving an explicit zero budget (ice:packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts:814-858; ice:packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts:1044-1073).

Thinking payloads are emitted only for reasoning models. Display defaults to summarized; disabling is omitted when thinkingLevelMap.off is null. Temperature is sent only when provided, thinking is not enabled and supportsTemperature allows it. Only string metadata.user_id is copied. Tool choice is passed as its protocol object. Default capability values include eager input, long cache, tool cache and temperature=true; affinity, empty signatures and strict tools=false; tool references use model identity/version inference. The enabled beta headers, auth identity, history and cache-marker rules are detailed in AI-022/024. Tests were read without execution; the live Opus smoke assertion expects {type:adaptive} alone at test line 48, which conflicts with the current summarized display field and is not accepted as evidence of a passing suite.

field_changes.before:
The Bedrock adapter builds shared inference fields and Claude-specific thinking controls before sending a command. It checks the hard output limit again after the payload hook, while model family and region determine the reasoning fields it emits.

Direct inference maxTokens is caller maxTokens clamped to hard limit, else Claude model.maxTokens clamped to hard limit, else only hard limit if present; non-Claude requests without a cap omit maxTokens. Temperature is included whenever defined, without a Bedrock-specific reasoning incompatibility gate. onPayload can replace the complete command input; afterward hardMaxOutputTokens is re-enforced inside inferenceConfig. requestMetadata is passed unchanged, with documented tag constraints not locally validated.

Claude recognition checks id for anthropic.claude or anthropic/claude and name additionally for claude. Version matching lowercases id and name and also normalizes spaces/underscore/dot/colon to hyphen. Adaptive list is opus4.6/4.7/4.8/5, sonnet4.6/5 and fable5. With reasoning requested and model.reasoning true, adaptive fields are thinking{type:adaptive, display} and output_config.effort. xhigh is forced native for opus4.7/4.8/5, sonnet5, fable5; otherwise string thinkingLevelMap entry wins, then minimal/low→low, medium→medium, high/default→high. Extended levels therefore need explicit map outside native-xhigh support.

Fixed-budget direct reasoning defaults minimal1024, low2048, medium8192, high16384; xhigh/max/ultra use high override/default. Non-Claude reasoning adds no additional fields. streamSimple uses shared base options; absent reasoning removes it, adaptive forwards levels/budgets, fixed-budget adjusts output then context/hard clamps and limits chosen budget to max(0, maxTokens-1024). field_changes.before:
Bedrock history conversion translates neutral messages into Converse content blocks and groups consecutive tool results. It normalizes IDs, validates image formats and chooses cache points according to the model and retention policy.

transformMessages first normalizes tool IDs by replacing nonalphanumeric/underscore/hyphen with underscore and truncating64. User strings require a nonblank sanitized text block or '<empty>'; arrays drop blank text and unknown block types but preserve supported images, adding placeholder only when all content disappears. Assistant empty arrays/all-filtered content are skipped. Text/thinking is surrogate-sanitized; blank thinking is omitted even if a signature exists. Claude thinking with missing/blank signature falls back to text, otherwise reasoningText carries text+signature; non-Claude reasoningText omits signature. Consecutive toolResult messages are combined into one user message, each toolUseId/status and ordered text/image content; empty result becomes '<empty>'. Images decode base64 into bytes and accept jpeg/jpg/png/gif/webp only; unknown MIME throws.

Retention explicit value wins, else scoped ICE_CACHE_RETENTION='long', else short. Cache support examines normalized id/name: a Claude reference plus fable/opus/sonnet5, any '-4-', claude3.7sonnet or 3.5haiku is allowed. AWS_BEDROCK_FORCE_CACHE='1' applies only when no Claude reference was found, not an override for an unsupported known Claude. Cache points follow a nonempty system text and the final message only if that final message is user; long adds ONE_HOUR TTL, none omits. Tools preserve full JSON schema under inputSchema.json, with native strict true only when constraint resolution and compat.supportsStrictMode allow. Empty tools or toolChoice='none' omit entire toolConfig. auto/any/named choices serialize distinct Converse toolChoice variants; unspecified choice omits only that field. No tool cache point is added.

field_changes.before:
The Bedrock stream mapper reconstructs indexed text, thinking and tool blocks from AWS events. It preserves raw stop reasons and rejects unfinished streams while carrying available usage and diagnostic metadata into the terminal result.

messageStart must be assistant and emits start. Tool start allocates an indexed tool block with empty arguments/scratch JSON; text/thinking blocks are lazily created on their first delta. Text deltas append and emit immediately, tool input reparses cumulative JSON, thinking text appends and emits while signature chunks append silently. contentBlockStop removes SDK index, emits the corresponding end event, and finalizes/removes tool scratch. Metadata overwrites input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite with value-or-zero and recalculates cost; total assignment at 617 is transport-redacted, so the unknown operand is not reconstructed, with visible fallback input+output. messageStop retains raw reason; end_turn/stop_sequence→stop, max_tokens/model_context_window_exceeded→length, tool_use→toolUse, other→error plus 'Provider stopped with: VALUE'. EOF requires a nonpending reason; abort is checked again after iteration. Error/aborted mapped stop triggers error terminal. Event union exceptions for internal/model-stream/validation/throttling/unavailable are thrown; processing continues after messageStop until iterator ends.

Catch preserves partial content, removes index and partialJson from every block, maps signal-aborted to aborted, formats normalized raw body/status when message omitted body and adds a data-retention documentation hint on matching text. SDK ServiceException names receive stable human prefixes used by downstream retry classification. A separate bedrock_response_failure diagnostic is emitted only for nonabort errors with known details: numeric status, Error.name ending Exception, request ID from error metadata or captured response. Header-derived strings are trim/nonempty/max200, dropped if oversized; bare object stream exceptions may supply only fallback request ID. Error message is not modified by diagnostics. Success cleanup relies on block-stop events and does not globally strip unfinished-block scratch at done, a source limitation to address deliberately.

field_changes.before:
Google thinking configuration depends on the model family and whether the caller uses direct or simple options. Explicit enable, disable, effort and token-budget values are translated separately, with the hard output limit bounding nonnegative thinking budgets.

Direct API applies thinking only for model.reasoning. Enabled emits includeThoughts=true and prefers explicit level over budget; nonnegative budget is min(budget, hardMaxOutputTokens) when hard cap exists, while negative dynamic budget is retained. An absent thinking option emits no thinkingConfig; explicit enabled=false emits a model-specific disable form. Simple absent reasoning always passes enabled=false. Simple requested reasoning is clampThinkingLevel(model, requested), coerces returned off to high, then casts to minimal/low/medium/high without a further runtime extended-level guard.

Gemini3 Pro matches /gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-pro/ and maps minimal/low→LOW, medium/high→HIGH; disable uses LOW without includeThoughts. Gemini3 Flash matches equivalent flash regex or exact gemini-flash-latest/gemini-flash-lite-latest, maps minimal/low/medium/high→MINIMAL/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH and disables with MINIMAL. Generative AI also recognizes /gemma-?4/: minimal/low→MINIMAL, medium/high→HIGH and disable MINIMAL; Vertex has no Gemma4 special case. Other models disable with thinkingBudget0.

Budget override by selected level wins. Case-sensitive id substring2.5-pro defaults128/2048/8192/32768. Generative AI2.5-flash-lite defaults512/2048/8192/24576 before its2.5-flash128/2048/8192/24576 branch; Vertex has only the latter flash branch, so flash-lite minimal differs128. Unknown budget family returns-1. Level helpers do not handle extended values at runtime if a custom model advertises them; the cast alone cannot clamp them, a source limitation. Output cap is separately enforced after payload hook, but thinking budget itself is not re-clamped after arbitrary hook replacement. The thinking-disable test spans other providers and uses credential-gated E2E assertions; it establishes intended cases only, not executed acceptance.

Tool text joins with newline. field_changes.before:
Mistral history conversion assigns request-local tool IDs and reuses each mapping for calls and results. It serializes neutral content into Mistral messages and clones tool schemas into ordinary JSON objects.

A request-local forward/reverse map guarantees repeated original IDs reuse the chosen ID and collisions with distinct originals retry. Derivation strips nonalphanumeric characters; attempt0 keeps that sanitized value only if length 9, otherwise hashes sanitized-or-original seed, or seed:attempt on collisions. shortHash is the exact two 32-bit UTF16-code-unit algorithm in utils/hash.ts using wrapping Math.imul, final mixing and concatenated unsigned base36 halves; the first 9 alphanumerics are taken. No padding is added, so the code truncates to at most 9 rather than proving fixed length for every possible hash. Preserve deterministic same-request mapping through transformMessages for calls and results.

User text is sanitized; array images become data-URL image_url chunks only when model supports images. Image-only unsupported content gets an explicit omission placeholder; an empty array without images is skipped. Assistant nonblank text and thinking become their respective content chunk kinds, tool calls are a separate toolCalls array with JSON arguments, and empty assistant messages are omitted. Thinking chunk output has no signature carrier. Tool results are individual role=tool messages with toolCallId/name and a text chunk first, then supported images. Text trims surrounding whitespace; errors prefix '[tool error] '. Unsupported accompanying images add an omission suffix; no text yields '(see attached image)', '(image omitted: model does not support images)' or '(no tool output)' as appropriate, with the same error prefix variants.

Each tool emits type:function, name, description, parameters and strict. Strict resolution assumes provider supports strict unconditionally; resulting true/false defaults false. parameters recursively clone arrays and Object.entries of objects, removing symbol keys at every visited level while retaining enumerable string-key schema structure. This avoids TypeBox metadata tripping SDK validation without JSON roundtrip semantics. The test verifies symbol removal and expects a request error at a local unreachable endpoint, not successful service execution.

field_changes.before: rust:crates/ice-agent/src/agent.rs:128-153; rust:crates/ice-agent/src/agent.rs:285-322; rust:crates/ice-agent/src/events.rs:134-165. field_changes.before:
waitForChildProcess listens for child error/exit/close and each pipe end/data event. Initially an absent pipe counts ended. On exit record code, finish immediately if both streams ended, otherwise arm a 100 ms idle timer. Every data event after exit resets that timer. Each stream end updates its flag and finishes when both ended. close finishes immediately. Finalize is once-only: clear timer/remove listeners, destroy both streams and resolve the code. A child error clears listeners and rejects. The same implementation applies on all platforms, although the inherited-stdio regression test is Windows-gated.

Continuous descendant output can indefinitely reset the post-exit idle timer; it is not a total100 ms deadline. Once idle elapses, later descendant output is intentionally discarded by destroying pipes. field_changes.before:
Both TS resource modules duplicate the same frontmatter parser. Normalize CRLF and lone CR to LF. Only startsWith("---") is tested, not a complete opening-fence line. Find the first substring newline+--- starting at offset3. If absent, return empty metadata and the entire normalized content untrimmed. Otherwise parse the slice from offset4 to the closing-fence start using yaml.parse; null/undefined becomes{}. Trim the body after the four-character closing marker. A closing marker with trailing text is accepted and that text enters the body. There is no explicit mapping-only check or local metadata/body size limit. A YAML parse exception is converted to parse_failed and the file is skipped. The installed YAML dependency owns its remaining syntax/alias behavior; no parser code was executed here.

field_changes.before:
Image processing first validates magic bytes, then normalizes/converts the MIME and optionally resizes the decoded image. Resizing uses a worker when possible and returns text-only omission if safe output cannot be produced.

Detection: JPEG begins FF D8 FF but rejects a fourth F7 marker; PNG requires at least 16 bytes and IHDR length 13, then rejects acTL before IDAT; GIF accepts the first three bytes 'GIF'; WebP requires RIFF and WEBP at offset8. BMP requires at least 26 bytes, consistent declared sizes, a DIB header12 or40–124, planes1 and bit depth1/4/8/16/24/32. Bounds-safe header readers return 0. The coding read's4100-byte probe may not see a later acTL chunk; the harness tests the complete bytes. Base64 uses the standard alphabet with padding and no line breaks.

processImage strips MIME parameters, trims/lowercases and maps image/jpg to image/jpeg. PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP are model-supported; other detected image types are converted to PNG via Photon. Conversion failure produces an omission message. autoResizeImages defaults true; false returns normalized supported bytes (or converted PNG) plus '[Image converted from <old> to <new>.]' when conversion happened. Resize failure/null also produces text-only omission, never an unsafe original fallback.

Resize defaults: maxWidth=maxHeight=2000, maxBytes=4.5*1024*1024 measured on base64 string length, jpegQuality80. Decode via Photon, apply EXIF orientation before measuring dimensions, and preserve original bytes if oriented dimensions and original base64 length are already within the limits. That early-return path keeps original encoded orientation even when a decoded orientation transform was applied. Otherwise constrain width then height with Math.round and Lanczos3. At each candidate dimension, resize from the original decoded image, try PNG first, then unique JPEG qualities [requestedQuality,85,70,55,40], and return the first candidate strictly smaller than maxBytes. It does not search for the smallest successful encoding. If none fits, floor both dimensions times 0.75 (minimum 1) and repeat down to1x1; failure returns null. WASM images are freed in finally.

The dimension hint is '[Image: original WxH, displayed at wxh. Multiply coordinates by SCALE to map to original image.]', SCALE=(originalWidth/width).toFixed(2); it is emitted whenever wasResized=true, including re-encoding without dimension change. EXIF support probes JPEG APP1 and WebP EXIF, TIFF orientation1–8; flips mutate in place, rotations allocate a new image. It does not scan PNG EXIF. The first JPEG APP1 without an Exif header ends the lookup; malformed/absent orientation defaults 1.

Worker transport copies caller bytes before transfer, validates result/error messages, rejects worker errors or exit before a result, and terminates the worker in finally. Bun compiled builds try './src/utils/image-resize-worker.ts', then TS/JS URL candidates, then in-process fallback. There is no explicit AbortSignal or timer. Photon module loading caches the promise (including failure), temporarily patches readFileSync to locate photon_rs_bg.wasm near the executable or cwd, and restores it after load. These packaging mechanics need not be reproduced by native Rust.

Both sort provider then id with English localeCompare, remove only model.headers, and use JSON.stringify([provider, id]) as the live key cursor. The cursor must identify an item in the current filtered list; unknown keys are not_found. Limit is1–1000 if given, otherwise all remaining items; nextCursor is emitted only with hasMore. get_models/get_providers OR the current runtime error with the adapter's remembered refresh failure; get_available_models has no error flag (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts:1330-1379; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/rpc-views.ts:139-170; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/rpc-pages.ts:11-27).

refresh_models first rejects busy when streaming/compacting, then denies allowNetwork=true whenever ICE_OFFLINE is defined, including an empty string, then rejects unknown provider ids before any refresh. It captures the current session, tracks its own AbortController and starts a default 10000 ms timer (input permits1–30000), then calls modelRuntime.refresh with allowNetwork default false, provider filter, force and signal. It refreshes selected-model metadata after the awaited result. The response is success=true even when refresh reports errors, aborts, times out or throws: data contains aborted, timedOut, generic provider/runtime error records with ModelsError.code or failed, and hasCatalogError. A thrown abort yields no errors; a nonaborted throw yields a generic runtime error. It emits models_changed with that same result before the response. Nonaborted results replace lastCatalogRefreshFailed with errors.length>0; aborted results only set it true when errors exist, never clear a prior failure. The result's error flag is ORed with that memory, reset on session replacement. Finally removes the controller and timer. abort_models_refresh aborts every tracked refresh controller and acknowledges without waiting for completion (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts:296-301; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts:1254-1328; RPC-020).

list_sessions defaults to cwd scope; all scope uses SessionManager.listAll() for the default session root or listAll(configuredSessionDir) for a custom root. Results sort modified descending, then path by ordinary string order, and an optional query (at most 256 code units) is trimmed/lowercased and matched against name/cwd/firstMessage/allMessagesText. A cursor is the exact path in that already-filtered current list; absent cursors fail not_found rather than restarting. Optional limit1–1000 bounds the remaining page; omission returns all. get_entries starts from SessionManager insertion order; since is an exact entry id whose preceding and matching items are skipped, with not_found when absent. It returns raw entries, current leafId, hasMore and conditional last-entry nextCursor; limit omission returns all. get_tree with no limit/cursor/parentId returns the complete nested tree and leafId. Any of those options switches to one-level pagination: parentId null/omitted selects roots, a nonnull id is found by an explicit stack walk or fails not_found, and the selected children use live id cursors and defaultlimit100. Each returned node has children=[] plus hasChildren, alongside parentId (null for roots), leafId and page fields. It slices the current messages (not a retained immutable copy), returns snapshot/hasMore and a conditional next cursor. The main runtime onThemePreview merely installs the supplied theme instance, and Apply invokes session.apply using the unchanged typed setting. Reset uses the base/dark palette, deletion requires confirm-delete, and errors stay in component state. Preview creation catches errors and calls onThemePreview with an in-memory Theme before rebuilding preview appearance; it does not write settings itself. The component retains original text separately from formatted display text, builds a background Box around Markdown and applies appearance styling without mutating the prompt. Rendering recomputes the width budget and rebuilds the box, then adds optional borders and OSC133 markers to the emitted rows.

Constructor defaults are Markdown theme from the global theme, outputPad1, no transformers and no appearance. getText returns the original text; setOutputPad/setAppearance rebuild immediately. With appearance, every `{message}` occurrence in format is replaced through split/join, the shared resolver supplies exact foreground/background/border colors and configured text styles, and appearance padding overrides outputPad. Without appearance, background is userMessageBg, foreground userMessageText and vertical padding0. Markdown is configured with preserveOrderedListMarkers:true and preserveBackslashEscapes:true, plus the user/false transformer context (TUI-028). Box padding is clamped nonnegative at construction (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/user-message.ts:31-102`).

render floors the requested width and clamps it to at least 1. Side borders reserve2 columns except none/top-bottom styles. Horizontal padding is limited to max(0, floor((safeWidth-sideWidth)/2)); vertical padding is used unchanged. The full-width branch renders the Box at safeWidth, clips/pads rows, wraps each row with side borders when present and finally clips/pads every returned row back to safeWidth. It therefore fits the final rows, but the Box is initially rendered at outer width rather than the reduced side-border content width; adding side borders clips the rendered rows instead of reflowing text at that smaller width. This source behavior is distinct from the comment claiming content is budgeted before borders (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/user-message.ts:104-145`).

fitToContent chooses min(maxWidth, longest visible source line+2*paddingX+sideWidth), using formatted raw source rather than rendered Markdown row widths. It renders at that outer target, slices side-border content to max(1, outerTarget-sideWidth), adds top/bottom and returns without the full-width branch's final clamp. For a one-column target with side borders, the helper still supplies two side glyphs and contentTarget remains1; this branch has an untested narrow-width overflow risk. The existing width1/2/3/10/30/80 matrix uses the default fitToContent:false; the fit-to-content test uses width 80. No runtime tests were executed (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/user-message.ts:122-135`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/user-message-presentation.ts:145-161`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-user-message-layout.test.ts:20-100`).

fitLineToWidth pads with spaces or slices by visible columns while preserving ANSI; zero requested width is allowed in this helper. fitTargetWidth measures each unwrapped source line. Exported fitLinesToContent measures already-rendered lines, clamps target to maxWidth-sideWidth and pads/truncates each, but the component's render path uses fitTargetWidth instead. The border helper supports none/single/double/round/bold/classic/single-double/double-single/top-bottom-single/top-bottom-double/top-bottom-bold; its mixed styles fall through to default horizontal/vertical glyphs, with the supplied mixed-style corner table, unlike the assistant helper's explicit mixed glyphs.

markOsc133Zone mutates the rows array. Empty rows remain empty; a single row begins A+B+C in order; multiple rows begin with A on the first and B+C on the last, never suffixing the line. Exact bytes are ESC]133;A BEL, ESC]133;B BEL and ESC]133;C BEL. User-message tests assert one-row compact output, marker order, background reset at line end and transformer context/invalidation; appearance tests cover format/style/color/width, not preservation of all text through side-border clipping.

Options default showImages=true, imageWidthCells=60, compact=false and no toolsAppearance. Unknown tools have no built-in definition and use the default shell unless an extension requests self. The default tree has a leading Spacer1 and Box1/1 with pending background; call and result Component references are retained separately for renderer reuse. A shared mutable state object survives both renderers. Context includes args, toolCallId, invalidate, lastComponent, state, cwd, executionStarted, argsComplete, isPartial, expanded, showImages and isError; invalidate clears component/render caches and requests a UI render. isPartial initially true. markExecutionStarted and setArgsComplete update display, while argument/result setters retain new values and clear display caches. updateResult defaults isPartial=false and replaces the result rather than appending text (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:40-238`).

Renderer exceptions fall back to generic call/result rendering. A result renderer receives content and details, with error state in context. The fallback call prints the tool name and JSON arguments; fallback results join textual blocks. Call and result renderer selection is independent, so a custom call renderer can retain built-in results and vice versa. Self shell omits generic box framing and can render no rows when its content is empty; it still uses the component's image children. Appearance affects state background/title/output styling but does not automatically impose all appearance-model geometry on an extension-owned component. Extension registration and transport remain EXT-owned.

Thus the source permits a prior or late conversion at the same ordinal to be reused for a later result. This is a TS state-lifetime limitation, not a contract to reproduce. Default/self shells include images when supported; compact rows include them only when expanded. Collapsed command displays its first logical line plus an ellipsis when multiline; expanded displays the complete command wrapped by the header renderer. Text joins text blocks, removes carriage returns and trims the end before splitting. An empty trailing-only output is distinct from missing result. The background preview branch tests property presence, whereas summarizeToolResult requires backgroundTaskId to be a string, so malformed metadata can fall through to a normal line-count summary. FooterDataProvider discovers Git metadata from its cwd and caches branch/status values separately. Branch changes are watched and debounced, while working-tree counts refresh only when requested by a footer consumer.

findGitPaths walks upward for .git. A directory uses .git/HEAD; a file beginning exactly 'gitdir: ' resolves its remainder relative to that directory, then resolves an optional commondir relative to the Git directory. Missing HEAD or a filesystem exception returns null immediately. An unrecognized .git file allows the walk to continue. The returned repoDir is the worktree/root used for Git subprocesses, commonGitDir locates shared reftable files, and headPath locates this worktree's HEAD. A regular 'ref: refs/heads/' HEAD preserves the full branch suffix. '.invalid' asks git --no-optional-locks symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD, synchronously on first getGitBranch and asynchronously during refresh; failure maps to 'detached'. Other readable HEAD contents also map to 'detached'; missing/read errors map to null. The symbolic-ref subprocess helpers do not set a timeout here (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/footer-data-provider.ts:16-81`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/footer-data-provider.ts:303-331`).

The branch watcher watches HEAD's parent directory to survive atomic replacement and reacts to missing filenames or exactly HEAD. On Linux with WSL_DISTRO_NAME/WSL_INTEROP and a /mnt/<drive> repo it additionally watchFiles HEAD every 1000 ms, comparing mtime/ctime/size. If a shared reftable directory exists, it watches that directory and, when tables.list exists, watches that file plus 250 ms metadata polling. Events schedule one 500 ms refresh; an event during an in-flight refresh marks a pending rerun. Callback notification occurs only when a previously known cached branch changes. Initial refresh can fill an undefined cache without notification. Watch errors close all watchers and schedule a 5000 ms retry; watch construction errors use the same error callback. field_changes.before:
FooterComponent receives a session and read-only data provider and computes its projection fresh on every render; invalidate and dispose are compatibility no-ops because the provider owns caching/watchers. setSession/setDataProvider replace dependencies, and setAppearance clones the supplied model.

formatTokens returns raw counts below 1000, one-decimal k below 10000, rounded k below1million, one-decimal M below10million and rounded M thereafter. formatCwdForFooter resolves cwd/home and uses path-relative containment, so a sibling merely sharing the home prefix is not abbreviated. It returns '~' for home itself and '~'+platform separator+relative path for descendants. sanitizeStatusText replaces CR/LF/tab with spaces, collapses literal spaces and trims; despite its broad comment it does not remove every other control sequence (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts:25-70`).

Legacy rendering aggregates all session entries on each render, including persisted subagent_usage, assistant usage, tool-result usage and branch/compaction usage. The latest assistant determines cache hit rate as cacheRead/(input+cacheRead+cacheWrite); subagent totals add cost/tokens but do not alter the session's current context estimate. Usage fields appear only for truthy counts; cache-hit percentage appears when cumulative read/write cache use exists and latest rate is known. Cost is fixed3 decimals and also shown at zero for OAuth-backed providers or kimi-coding, with '(sub)'. A child-cost hint is inserted beside total cost before the subscription marker only when estimated width also leaves room for the model. Current context uses session.getContextUsage separately, falls back to model contextWindow, marks explicit percent:null as '?', and otherwise defaults missing percent to0.0. Thresholds strictly above70 and90 use warning/error, and auto compaction appends '(auto)'. Experimental mode adds xp (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts:305-406`).

The first legacy row is cwd, optional branch in parentheses and optional session name; it is width-truncated. The second puts usage/context left and model plus reasoning level right, with at least 2 spaces. A provider prefix is attempted only when availableProviderCount>1 and dropped first if it does not fit. Left stats are clipped before the right side gets its remaining budget; if no room remains, the model disappears. Extension status values sorted by localeCompare(key) form an optional third row. A combined subagent/notices badge may replace the right side of row1 via placeRight; if the badge plus 2 exceeds width it is omitted rather than overflowing.

Appearance differs from the default only when JSON.stringify differs. A color-only override retains compact layout when compact style is selected; changes in order, visible or separator force customized multirow layout. Customized primary fields are cwd/branch/session; secondary fields are usage/cache/cost/context/provider/model/thinking; extension values have their own row. Within each group appearance.order and visible select fields, then trailing fields are popped until one or more fit and the final string is clipped. The groups remain separate even if the order interleaves their IDs. Context always uses strict numeric-percent detection ('?' otherwise), with threshold colors overriding appearance colors; other fields use primary/secondary text presentation. Experimental xp joins usage. Extension styling is independent, and the subagent/notices overlay still applies after layout (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts:482-591`).

Read tests cover wide names/model/provider text, all-entry cost totals, subagent cost without context inflation, hint omission at narrow widths, subscription marker placement, cache-hit rate, safety colors and badge clipping. They do not turn the comments about native unknown context into an implementation guarantee.

field_changes.before:
Compact footer builds left/right StatusSegment arrays, assigns priorities and delegates width allocation to layoutStatusLine. Color-only footer appearance overrides preserve this compact route; structural field customization selects TUI-038's multirow layout instead.

Left segments are execution mode 'ice-mode' plus elevated capabilities at required priority100, cwd priority60 with middle shrink/min16, branch priority65 with shrink/min12 plus unchanged counts, session name30 and other extension statuses20. Capabilities use error color and abbreviate external→ext; other status keys are sorted, sanitized and blank values removed. Git ahead uses success, behind/dirty warning and zero counts disappear. Branch shrinking cuts its label while retaining the count suffix. Right segments are model/thinking70, context90, active shells95, subagent segment variable priority and notices100. Context appears only for a positive window, rounds a numeric percent to an integer and otherwise shows '?', and uses strict >70/>90 warning/error thresholds (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts:177-265`).

The shell segment appears only when background count>0, pluralizes shells and optional watches, and links to OPEN_SHELLS_URL. The subagent segment exists whenever an overview exists: 'agents running/max' or 'agents off', then nonzero queued count and the count of children whose state is idle. Pending approvals append a warning label. Activity uses primary color, idle uses secondary. Priority is 100 with approvals,96 with running/queued activity and 65 otherwise; the segment links to OPEN_AGENTS_URL. Notices count warning+error, ignore informational/update counts, and use error color when any error exists. These are display callbacks, not lifecycle or policy implementations (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts:247-303`).

layoutStatusLine copies segments and uses a 2-column gap. While overflow remains it chooses the lowest-priority eligible segment, scanning left then right with stable ties. A shrink callback is attempted once toward the minimum width needed, clamped to minWidth(default 1), and then removed even if it failed to shorten. Before dropping a previously shortened target it tries another available shrink candidate. Segments at priority>=100 are never dropped, though they may shrink. Nonrequired targets are removed until the row fits or only required content remains. A fitting row fills intervening spaces to width; if required content still overflows, left and right are clipped separately onto two rows, right-aligned on its row, and blank rows removed. No segment mutation leaks back to the caller. A callback that returns an oversized minimum can still be dropped or clipped by the final path (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/status-line.ts:13-84`).

The middleTruncate helper used for cwd budgets visible cells but slices JS UTF-16 code units, so a wide-character path can exceed the requested cell budget or split a surrogate pair; this is documented in TUI-040 and should be corrected rather than copied. Tests cover count preservation beside long paths, normal120-column badge combinations, widths40/60/80, color-only customization, required approvals and disabled agents. They do not establish correctness for every Unicode shrink callback.

Each installs one new resolver pair: a concurrent second prompt would overwrite the first, and these methods do not check already-aborted signal. showDetails clears and replaces content, while showInfo/showWaiting/showProgress append messages and optional links/hints without a history cap. Text defaults text='', paddingX=1, paddingY=1, optional custom background. Raw empty or trim-empty text renders no rows. It expands every tab to 3 spaces before wrapping, uses max(1, width-2*paddingX), surrounds each wrapped row with both horizontal margins and pads to width, then adds width-filled top/bottom rows. An optional bgFn applies through background-reset-aware utility. Its cache keys text and width; setText, setCustomBgFn and invalidate clear it. Caller-owned mutable background closures require invalidation if behavior changes without the setter.

Box defaults padding1/1, returns no rows for no children or all-empty child output, renders children at max(1, width-2*paddingX), prepends left padding then pads/backgrounds each row. Cache compares width, exact rendered child lines and bgFn('test') sample; it still renders children before cache lookup. setBgFn relies on sampling rather than immediate invalidation; invalidate cascades. removeChild removes only the first identity match. There is no intrinsic border in Box.

Spacer defaults 1 empty row and supports setLines; it is unpadded and uncached. TruncatedText defaults zero margins, selects text before the first LF only, truncates at max(1, width-2*paddingX), surrounds/pads to full width and adds width-filled vertical rows. Empty text still renders one padded content row. These minimum-content-width policies can exceed an extremely narrow outer width when margins alone do not fit; do not claim hard clipping universally.

The unpadded Container exposes a mutable children array; addChild appends, removeChild deletes the first identity match, clear replaces the array, render concatenates every child at the same width, and invalidate calls optional child invalidation. It adds no layout sizing or implicit redraw.

field_changes.before:
The evaluator combines all matching rules using deny before ask before allow, then applies opaque-command and mode ceilings. A tool invocation is only as permissive as its most restrictive subject. Shell processing is a bounded textual approximation rather than a shell parser.

A rule is a tool glob, optionally followed by a 1..512-character parenthesized subject glob; tool syntax is '*' or an alphabetic first character followed by at most 127 alphanumeric, underscore, dot, asterisk orhyphen characters. parsePermissionRule does not trim. Path glob '*' stays inside one component, '**' crosses components and '**/' also matches no prefix; '?' is one nonseparator character. Nonpath '*' matches any characters across newlines, while '?' uses regex dot. Matching is anchored. Decisions carry matching origin scope(builtin, managed, user, project, cli, session) and carrier(settings, agent-definition, compat-definition, flag, grant). No matching rule uses the supplied fallback. Stable sorting preserves equal-ranked match order.

read/grep/find/ls extract a read path; edit/write extract edit-write. A nonempty string args.path resolves lexically against cwd, otherwise '.'. In-cwd subjects use relative slash paths; outside paths use absolute values and add an external_directory subject. Unknown or unclassified adapters are mutation-adapter, never read. agent tasks contribute delegation subjects using the requested agent names. Bash splits on &&,||, semicolon, newline, unpaired '&' and '|', excluding descriptor operators by the literal regex; it does not honor shell quotes. Any command/process substitution syntax ($(...), backticks,<(,>()) marks every command fragment opaque. File output redirection marks that fragment opaque after allowing descriptor duplication and recognized /dev/null redirection; this cannot serve as complete shell-language validation.

A parent owner has a configurable admission pool. Accepted turn intent is durable before admission, while timers start only after a permit is acquired. An uncooperative aborted turn is fenced from later result publication.

runTurn rejects unknown, nonresident, already-running or patch-closed children despite its older 'never throws' comment. This acknowledgement can precede a concurrency slot. acquire loops until a permit is available; waiting promises are queued and a release wakes one. A wake is not a reserved permit, so a newcomer can win the next acquisition; do not claim strict FIFO admission. Caller abort removes a queued waiter. No queue timeout runs before admission, and the pool/maxConcurrent is captured when the owner is constructed rather than rebuilt on every settings change.

After admission, start wall and idle deadlines, default 1800000 ms and 600000 ms, plus an idle alert at min(configured alert, floor(idleTimeout/2)); configured0 disables the alert. Bash still has its tool ceiling and the child wall deadline, and still receives idle alerts. Track startedAt, lastActivityAt, current tool/arguments for status; send at most one alert per quiet stretch. The alert is informational, delivered as steer when the parent is busy and nextTurn when idle.

Caller cancellation is attached after the internal abort-grace listener, then pre-aborted signals are applied. Expiry records the deadline reason and aborts. After 10000 ms without settlement, mark finishClaimed/fenced, clear timers, release the admission permit once, clear foreground and record abandoned with explicit unknown last-tool effects. The underlying promise may still be running; resident.running remains until its real settlement, and late settlement cannot record a second outcome. This releases TypeScript concurrency before every underlying effect is known to stop. Native cleanup-permit retention is a stronger resource bound worth preserving.

On admitted start, recheck authority, persist running, install the bounded-turn wrapper and emit started observation. Queued cancellation reports cancelled and may delete a never-run child without a patch. Provider stop, error, length and empty-text outcomes are classified separately; cancellation or deadline overrides completion. Finalization claims the outcome before asynchronous acceptance hooks, preventing grace from double-publishing while bookkeeping completes. Timers/listeners/budget state and permits are cleaned up. Idle children retire after 30000 ms if not displayed, foreground, running or in a patch operation; excess idle residents are parked oldest-first beyond8, and that separate excess-parking path does not consult displayed status.

During the bounded run, disable automatic session retry and compaction and save prior settings/hooks/stream state. Restore them on disposal. The timeout calls session.abort; a noncooperative prompt can still outlive that local await, with outer turn cancellation/abandonment providing the broader terminal path. Never describe the wrap-up as proof that every tool or provider stopped.

field_changes.before:
Revival reopens the child's durable transcript and frozen contract, checks ownership/hash/current authority and worktree existence/ownership, resolves the frozen model, and only then attaches a resident session. Blocked reasons remain visible without manufacturing a live handle.

continueChild refuses a closed patch or patch operation, revives parked/blocked children and runs a new turn. It may add task-local acceptance to the frozen baseline but cannot replace model, scope, tools, isolation or output schema. Resume-added criteria do not mutate the persistent baseline: a later turn without those additions requires only the original criteria. Interrupted revival adds a recovery notice listing unmatched tool calls and their unknown effects; it does not replay them. One child cannot run two turns concurrently.

send(message) while running uses session.steer; send(followup) queues session.followUp. For an idle child, message revives if needed and appends a pending note without starting provider work; followup starts a new background turn. interrupt aborts, awaits resident.running, then starts the follow-up. That await is unbounded for an uncooperative underlying promise, unlike stop. stop aborts and waits at most 10500 ms for a running turn; the run's10000ms grace can report abandoned. detachToBackground only changes resident foreground/background bookkeeping; it does not itself detach a caller AbortSignal already installed by runTurn.

Delete refuses applying/rollback_conflict or another patch operation, stops the child, writes the registry tombstone before disposal/cleanup, removes an owned worktree and releases output artifacts. Disposal can still await session.abort, so delete is not globally bounded merely because stop is. Shutdown closes the owner, cancels broker requests/timers and all resident controllers, waits for running turns up to 10500 ms and disposeAll up to 10000 ms, then clears owner state. Stale factory/revival handles are disposed rather than reattached. Closing-session cancellation becomes interrupted for restart delivery.

outputOf returns a clone of the saved latest result. Interrupted state without a valid saved result returns undefined instead of recycling a previous verified answer. Legacy transcript fallback takes the latest nonempty assistant text, redacts and caps it at 48 KiB, and labels it unverified_plain with cumulative usage. A result snapshot can remain available after an unchanged worktree has been cleaned, even though its previously checked evidence paths no longer exist.

field_changes.before:
Runtime apply requires a trusted parent in build mode, active agent_patch, an open patch and explicit allow for every affected parent write; ask is not silently approved. It validates the inspected artifact and rejects child changes made after inspection.

Parent authority is checked before preparation, immediately before writing and after verification. Resume/delete are blocked while integration is in progress. A failed verification reopens the patch; applied/empty parks the child with best-effort cleanup. Reject records its terminal state before owned force-removal.

The integration helper obtains a synthetic repository lock through the shared in-process mutation queue, then sorted individual path locks. These coordinate application tools, not unrelated OS writers. An empty delta returns empty. Reject out-of-scope/protected paths, symlink leaves in baseline/final state, unsupported file/directory replacements and configured external Git merge drivers. Capture real-index hash and current raw parent tree. If the parent diverged from the child baseline, construct ours/theirs commits with a common baseline and use git merge-tree --write-tree --no-messages --merge-base; a conflict returns bounded4096-character diagnostics before parent writes. The resulting changed paths must be a subset of the child's delta; no new merge-introduced paths are accepted.

Capture regular-file preimages with raw blob/mode checks. Preserve existing non-executable mode bits while taking the resulting Git executable bit; the tests include0600→0711. Combined preimage/postimage bytes must fit16MiB. Under locks recheck index and preimages; drift before writes returns changed_during_apply with the path or Git index. Reauthorize, then invoke beforeWrite to durably publish recovery data/applying state. For each path, recheck expected current contents and use an exclusive temporary file, chmod and rename, or delete the expected regular file. Track only writes that actually completed. Optional verification must return passed; afterward reauthorize and verify all postimages, unchanged real index and complete parent snapshot==result tree. Commit the durable applied result before discarding preimages. Without a verifier, successful apply remains unverified=true.

On any failure, walk completed writes in reverse. Restore only when current content still equals the transaction's expected postimage; a path already equal to its preimage needs no work. Preserve newer content and report rollback_conflict with affected paths rather than overwriting it. Otherwise report verification_failed after rollback. Do not restore a changed index or unrelated external writes; created empty directories may remain. Thus the contract is conflict-preserving best-effort file rollback, not an atomic repository transaction. Tests cover nonoverlapping dirty-parent merge, conflicts, verification rollback, index mutation during verification and newer-file preservation.

field_changes.before:
The ice agents dispatch runs before normal startup and supports list [--json], validate [paths...] and prune [--apply] [--json]; unknown command/options return exit 2. List returns 0 and renders active/shadowed/disabled definitions and discovery issues, or equivalent JSON.

It does not fail the exit code for invalid settings and does not include settings diagnostics as a substitute for validation. Validate with no paths combines scoped settings diagnostics and invalid definitions: errors return 1, deprecation warnings alone0, and an untrusted definition is not inherently malformed. Explicit non-flag paths are read and parsed as native user definitions; those reads have no additional CLI file-size bound, non-agent Markdown succeeds, invalid/unreadable files fail, and this branch does not also perform global catalog/settings validation.

Definition creation validates the native lowercase name, requires trust when creating in the project directory, refuses an existing destination, creates the directory and writes with wx so it never overwrites. Global creation has no extra project-trust requirement. The interactive /agents new command uses this helper.

Pruning scans one level of plain session directories beneath sessionsRoot. It collects live parent IDs by the filename pattern _([^_]+)\.jsonl$ across those directories, without an is-file test for the matching entry. It considers plain subagents/<parentId> folders orphaned only if that ID is absent everywhere. A recent folder or direct child mtime within 10 minutes holds the folder; this is not a recursive newest-descendant scan. It counts direct transcript JSONL files and worktree entries, excluding owner marker files. Every candidate worktree must be plain, have matching ownership metadata and have no delta from its baseline. Unknown, malformed, changed or failed worktrees hold the whole parent folder.

Default is deletion-free planning; --apply removes each verified owned clean worktree through Git, then removes the lexically direct orphan folder recursively. Partial failures become keep reasons and preserve the remainder. Other parents and changed worktrees are retained. The dry-run uses worktreeHasChanges→snapshotWorktree, which can write Git objects and a temporary index: it is not a fully read-only command, although it performs no planned deletions. The audit did not invoke it. The code checks the scanned entries, but does not establish that every ancestor of sessionsRoot is nonsymlink.

field_changes.before:
createIceSubagents builds a hidden inline ice-subagents extension at before-user priority, attaches an IceAgentViewBridge and exposes attach, overview and respondToApproval; subscriptions are available through the bridge. Options provide plan/build mode, explicit agents, host hook handlers, MCP adapter and agent directory; mode defaults to plan.

Early overview access must use the actual parent session settings and trust even before session_start, rather than constructing defaults. The wrapper does not independently require a persistent session before construction; the runtime's durable barrier rejects unsupported launches later. In headless build mode an ask permission fails closed without a foreground approval UI/inbox, while an explicit user allow rule may grant the corresponding write.

Trusted extensions find a version 1 controller on their shared events owner using Symbol.for("ice.subagents.controller.v1"). Registration defines a configurable owner property and replaces any previous controller. Its cleanup removes the property only if it still points to the same controller, so stale cleanup cannot erase a replacement. No process-global singleton is required.

start accepts the agent task schema but forbids resume, checks an already-aborted signal, normalizes context into the prompt, calls the normal runtime launch/preflight/approval path, captures the resident frozen model and calls onLaunched before running. runTurn is foreground:true, returns directly to the caller and does not enqueue parent-conversation completion delivery. Return id, agent, frozen {provider, id}, outcome, bounded text/truncated/error, input/output/cache read/cache write/cost usage, optional patchState, verified structured payload and any validation findings. The signal is passed to runTurn but not runtime.launch: cancellation arriving during launch approval does not itself cancel that pending launch. A throwing onLaunched callback can leave an accepted resident child before its first turn; record that behavior instead of promising transactional callback cleanup.

stop delegates to runtime.stop. openPatches lists this owner's patchState=open children. preview computes the open child delta without inspecting/pinning it, returning worktree root, changed paths, display patch and truncated flag. The default cap is64KiB, implemented by raw-byte subarray followed by UTF-8 decoding, so it can replace a cut multibyte character; maxBytes is not independently schema-validated. Another child may read an owner's open patch worktree when its allowed scope includes it, while the protected-path guard forbids writing there. Integration still requires ordinary agent_patch inspect/apply.

field_changes.before:
The inline ice-subagents extension registers agent, agent_control and agent_patch; patch execution is sequential. Caught model-facing errors become normal text/details rather than automatically setting isError.

It registers the agents string flag and sub-yolo boolean flag, uses the current parent mode as build only when explicitly build, and combines sub-yolo input with the startup authorization contract. Settings are memoized by serialized global/project ice.subagents values and current trust. Host-pinned hook/MCP/verifier adapters are supplied through the extension options rather than arbitrary model arguments.

Parent binding follows the latest extension context and attached bridge. A shut-down-parent WeakSet prevents later callbacks from journaling against a closed parent; resume/switch rebinds to the new parent before launch. session_start invalidates configuration cache, initializes/restores runtime ownership, reconnects registry/live controls and prepares catalog/roster delivery. Startup/resume may flush persisted interruption/completion notices; a forced model turn occurs only when hasUI and pending interruption are both true. New/fork initialization does not replay another owner's work. Fork reports the count of children still owned by the original session rather than adopting them.

before_agent_start injects the incremental agent listing and, after startup/resume/compaction, a roster of the last 20 depth-zero children with description prefixes80 characters. The combined catalog/roster text is not recapped as a whole. Ordinary repeat turns suppress unchanged catalog/roster data; compaction makes it eligible again. message_end confirms posted completion delivery, and session_compact/agent_settled flush pending idle deliveries. session_shutdown cancels/settles the runtime, removes controller/listener bindings and prevents stale callbacks from acquiring the departed owner. The exact durable delivery transaction and crash window are SUB-017.

Registry event serialization emits subagent_start, subagent_turn_start, subagent_turn_end (with blocked-transition exceptions), subagent_parked, subagent_revived, subagent_blocked, subagent_end, subagent_interrupted and subagent_patch; completion notification is a separate path. Events use the ice:subagent channel and metadata derived from the child record, including type, childId, agent, ownerSessionId, depth, state, optional lastTurnOutcome and optional patchState; no name or usage is added by lifecycleEvents/completionEvent. They do not include raw task prompts or raw report output; bounds come from validated contracts/record fields, not a generic serializer-wide cap.

Foreground approval presents Allow once, an offered allow-session rule, or Deny. Background requests surface through the owner inbox and event/UI notifications; no UI/inbox means deny. The view bridge exposes owner overview, approval answers, durable/live messages and stop/resume/delete/send. Runtime errors for unknown/cross-owner messages return undefined through the bridge. The command layer opens /agents hub and native definition creation. Main ice.ts loads the inline extension and MCP bridge before normal execution, with session shutdown releasing the parent MCP proxy binding.

completionEvent emits subagent_completion_queued with state=idle and the completion outcome. The extension separately emits subagent_permission_request with depth=0, state=blocked and the requested tool after in-memory per-request announcement suppression. The lifecycle union permits both, but lifecycleEvents alone does not emit them.

Known display IDs may be selected/cycled; switching releases previous control. Taking control requires a live working control object; sending interactive input requires controlled mode. Historical views are always read-only. Parent replacement returns display to parent and releases control, but setParentSession does not itself clear the historical map. Disconnect releases controls/live bindings; it is not a claim that every history/control-source reference is erased. Owner checks are enforced by the supplied runtime source, not by arbitrary descriptor IDs alone.

Historical snapshots clone/redact/deep-freeze at most the last 96 source messages, skipping a message over 16 KiB and stopping at an aggregate256KiB. Retain at most 32 historical children with oldest-history eviction and accompanying UI state cleanup. Parent transcript query returns undefined; child transcript retrieval prefers live bounded messages, then the durable runtime control source, then historical snapshots. Observer exceptions are swallowed, unknown display IDs fail softly, overview source errors yield undefined, and subscribers receive updates without being allowed to break the runtime.

field_changes.before:
The pre-startup --import-agent-pack flag accepts one nonempty path in separate or equals form; a resolved value beginning with a dash is not accepted in either form. Success prints the import report and exits0 even when everything was skipped; an exception exits1.

Import scans source/.claude/agents recursively in lexical order, skips child symlinks, accepts case-insensitive .md and rejects more than 128 discovered files. The root stat follows a symlink; this is not a promise that every source ancestor is nonsymlink. The target directory may be created before any candidate validates.

Skip README/index files, files over 64 KiB, duplicate content SHA, malformed frontmatter, missing name/description and empty body. Deduplication records the content hash before later parse checks. Slugify the foreign name to lowercase alphanumeric/hyphen, trim to 56 characters, then add a ruflo prefix within 64. Resolve collisions by source-relative path and then an 8-hex hash suffix. Existing exact generated content is already-imported; differing content is a conflict and is not overwritten. The final write uses 0600 after the existence check but not exclusive wx, leaving an external-writer race.

Map Read/read_file to read, Grep/search/search_files to grep, Find/glob/list_files to find, and ls/list to ls. Unknown tools are reported with bounded names; if no known tools remain, use the four read-only tools. Foreign metadata outside name/description/tools/model is reported unsupported, and model is ignored. The generated description uses a 512-code-unit prefix, carries pack/path/content-SHA provenance and frames the body as untrusted source text. A file can appear in both imported and unsupported-metadata reporting; JSON lists are bounded by the 128-file scan.

Source-read defect: nativeMarkdown unconditionally emits ice-unsafe-host-exec: allowed at ice-agent-packs.ts148. The current strict native definition parser rejects that removed key. Therefore a successfully written imported profile can be unusable in active V2 discovery; do not count this converter as a working V2 import path solely because files are created. field_changes.before:
The authentication layer gives providers typed prompts, notifications and cancellation, with lazy loading of concrete OAuth flows. Shared helpers generate PKCE material, schedule device polling and render callback pages.

AuthPrompt is text|secret|select|manual_code with message and optional per-prompt AbortSignal; text/secret/manual may have placeholder, select has readonly id/label/description choices and resolves an ID string. AuthEvent is info(message, links?), auth_url(url, instructions?), device_code(userCode, verificationUri, intervalSeconds?, expiresInSeconds?), progress(message). The whole interaction signal is normalized before provider login. API-key auth may omit login for ambient-only readiness and may supply a side-effect-free check separately from resolve; OAuth splits login, refresh(credential, signal), toAuth(credential), allowing store-owned refresh exclusion (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/types.ts:117-237).

lazyOAuth exposes name/loginLabel without loading and caches the first loader Promise, including a rejected one. OAuth loader imports through a variable module specifier, rewriting trailing .ts→.js only when import.meta.url ends in .js, so browser bundlers do not statically chase Node callback-server modules. registerBundledOAuthFlowLoaders replaces a module-global loader set; every flow loader uses it when present, otherwise dynamic import. bun-oauth installs seven static loaders for Anthropic, Codex, Copilot, OpenRouter, Kimi, xAI, Radius; Radius gets name/gateway options (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/helpers.ts:34-54; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/load.ts:1-68; ice:packages/ai/src/bun-oauth.ts:1-22).

PKCE generates32 cryptographically random bytes, unpadded base64url verifier, then SHA-256 of its UTF-8 string and unpadded base64url challenge. Shared device polling uses deadline Date.now()+expiresInSeconds*1000 when typeof number, otherwise Infinity; initial interval max(1000, floor((intervalSeconds??5)*1000)). Default is immediate first poll; waitBeforeFirstPoll sleeps min(interval, remaining) first. While Date.now()<deadline it checks abort, awaits poll, immediately returns complete or throws failed message. slow_down uses a finite positive server interval directly (at least 1000 ms), otherwise adds5000ms; it may therefore reduce a previous larger interval when the server says so. Pending/slow-down sleeps at most remaining deadline. No helper timeout races an in-flight poll and a complete result is returned before another deadline/abort check. Sleep cancellation throws Error('Login cancelled'); timeout distinguishes ordinary `Device flow timed out` from the detailed clock-drift/WSL/VM guidance after any slow_down (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/pkce.ts:1-35; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/device-code.ts:1-98).

Shared callback pages escape &,<,>, double quote, single quote for title/heading/message/details, render dark success/failure HTML and pre-wrap optional error details. They contain no automatic redirect/script. Individual flows choose status/cache headers and own server lifetime (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/oauth-page.ts:1-109). Dedicated poll tests inspect immediate/delayed first call, +5 seconds and server interval, and abortable wait; they were read, not executed (ice:packages/ai/test/oauth-device-code.test.ts:11-144).

OpenRouter login exchanges a one-use PKCE authorization for a permanent API key. Browser callbacks and manual input share ownership of the exchange, and the resulting credential is shared by text and image providers.

Login generates PKCE plus random callback path /oauth/callback/<UUID>, binds an ephemeral port 0 on current ICE_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST||127.0.0.1 and advertises that host/actual port. The authorize URL https://openrouter.ai/auth receives callback_url, code_challenge, code_challenge_method:S256; there is no separate OAuth state parameter. It emits listening progress then auth_url, then races manual_code prompt against a callback that performs the exchange itself (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:20-43; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:135-240; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:242-298).

Callback accepts only GET with exact unpredictable path; other requests404. claimed/settled callback409 prevents duplicate exchanges. OAuth error400 settles rejection; missing code400 leaves wait open. First valid code claims exchange, success page200 and credential settlement; exchange failure502 and login rejection. Every page sets content-type HTML UTF-8 and cache-control:no-store. finish settles once, clears timer/listener and closes server. Initial bind errors reject; post-listen server errors settle. A 5-minute timer fails pending login. User abort rejects Login cancelled. Manual completion/error hands off only if callback has not claimed exchange; after callback result a recorded manualError still takes precedence. finally aborts the manual prompt and closes the server. Manual parser trims URL/query code or bare code, with no #state form; empty/missing code rejects (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:45-67; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:135-298).

Exchange POSTs JSON {code, code_verifier, code_challenge_method:S256}, JSON Accept/content-type, with a dedicated30s controller linked to caller; cancellation and timeout get distinct exact messages. TOKEN_URL literal is redacted both in implementation21 and test9, so its exact endpoint remains an evidence limitation rather than inferred from memory. Success JSON must be a nonarray object with nonempty string key; malformed successful JSON and absent key have distinct errors. Non-OK detail precedence is error_description→message→string error→nested error.message, included in `OpenRouter OAuth key exchange failed (HTTP <status>)`. Credential is type:oauth, access:key, refresh:"", expires:Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. refresh returns the same credential unchanged, ignoring its signal; toAuth returns access as apiKey (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:69-133; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:301-311).

Tests specify shared stored OAuth key for text/images, PKCE digest, one exchange despite duplicate callback, callback502 plus login failure, manual URL/bare code, cancellation, no-key error and configured callback host; source was read, not run (ice:packages/ai/test/openrouter-oauth.test.ts:29-320).

Kimi Code login uses device authorization with a bounded lifetime for each request. Refresh has its own selective retry policy and returns an Authorization header for inference.

Client ID is 17e5f671-d194-4dfb-9706-5516cb48c098. Each device, poll and refresh fetch receives AbortSignal.any of caller signal and a fresh30-second timeout. Device initiation POSTs form client_id to /api/oauth/device_authorization with JSON Accept; both verification URLs must parse as HTTP(S), though the original strings are retained, and device/user code need only have string type. Finite positive expires_in/interval are used; otherwise defaults 900 seconds and 5 seconds. The UI receives verification_uri_complete. Polling waits before its first request and POSTs client_id, device_code, device grant to /api/oauth/token (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/kimi-coding.ts:13-117; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/kimi-coding.ts:141-164; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/kimi-coding.ts:281-292).

Polling HTTP>=500 fails immediately with status and body. Successful access-token responses still require nonempty access and refresh tokens and finite positive expires_in. authorization_pending continues; slow_down supplies a positive numeric interval or lets the common helper add5seconds; expired_token and access_denied have distinct user-facing errors. Other failures include status and string error/description. Tokens expire at Date.now()+expires_in*1000 without an OAuth-flow skew (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/kimi-coding.ts:119-207).

The source comment saying Models clears dead credentials is stale: this function only throws, while the authoritative resolver leaves stored credentials unchanged on refresh failure (AUTH-004; Models collection integration AI-002) (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/kimi-coding.ts:209-279).

field_changes.before:
Radius supports browser and device-code login against a configured gateway. Browser authorization uses discovery, while token exchange, device polling and refresh use fixed paths beneath that gateway.

createRadiusOAuth receives name and gateway, normalizes the gateway using the Radius helper, and exposes a browser-first select prompt with values browser and device-code (hyphenated). Client ID remains pi-gateway; scope gateway offline_access. Browser login alone GETs <gateway>/v1/oauth for authorizationEndpoint and requires only a string; URL construction happens later without the stricter verification-URL checks used by other flows. It creates PKCE and UUID state, sets response_type:code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, code_challenge, code_challenge_method:S256, handoff:url, state, replacing any existing authorization search (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:26-67; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:221-270; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:353-389).

The browser callback is fixed http://127.0.0.1:1456/oauth/callback, with no ICE_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST override and no manual-code fallback. Wrong path404, wrong state400, provider error400 settles null, missing code400 leaves the wait open, valid code200 settles. Abort settles null; binding error resolves a no-op callback server whose wait returns null. Login translates absent code to OAuth callback did not complete unless aborted, which becomes Login cancelled. Finally always closes. There is no adapter timer bounding the browser wait (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:148-219; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:221-270).

Authorization-code exchange, device polling and refresh always use <gateway>/v1/oauth/token, never a token URL from discovery. They POST form data with JSON Accept and caller signal, with no added request timeout. Non-OK errors become OAuthResponseError carrying status and OAuth error; detail comes from error/description or status, with non-JSON text accepted as description. Successful token payload is cast without the strict runtime access/refresh/lifetime checks of xAI/Kimi; stored fields are access_token, refresh_token, expiry now+expires_in*1000−60000, scope (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:69-146).

Device initiation POSTs client_id/scope to <gateway>/v1/oauth/device and checks only truthiness of device_code, user_code, verification_uri, expires_in. It does not validate their runtime types, positive finite expiry or URL scheme. Device-code UI receives the raw URI. Polling starts immediately, forwards device grant/client/device code to the direct gateway token endpoint, treats OAuthResponseError authorization_pending and slow_down specially, and emits separate expired/denied messages. Refresh uses refresh grant directly against the gateway without discovery; toAuth returns apiKey access (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:272-351; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:390-403).

Source-read tests establish direct gateway endpoints for device and refresh, browser-only discovery and rejection of discovery lacking authorizationEndpoint; no requests were actually executed (ice:packages/ai/test/radius-oauth.test.ts:27-128).

field_changes.before:
The Providers settings submenu shows catalog counts and lets a user refetch one provider. One shared admission flag prevents overlapping refetches while list and detail navigation remain available.

The extension stores the latest session_start context and registers settings group/id `providers`. Opening before a session context exists returns a Providers unavailable view with the select-cancel key returning to the caller. Otherwise summaries come from modelRegistry.getRuntime(), and refetch uses getAgentDir(), ctx.modelRegistry.refresh, runtime.getModels(id).length and the caller's signal (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider-settings.ts:181-234).

The submenu shallow-copies summaries and initially shows a provider list. Each label is the provider id, not its display name; description is `<count> models · <baseUrl ?? built-in>`. Primary column min/max widths are12/32, visible rows are min(count,10). Empty summaries show No providers configured and cancel-key handling. Selecting a row shows a read-only Models count plus Refetch catalog with currentValue run or working; Esc from detail returns to the list. Returning to the list clears selectedProviderId (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider-settings.ts:22-105; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider-settings.ts:107-150).

One submenu-wide refetching boolean rejects all overlapping requests, including another provider. On start it sets status key `ice-providers` to `Refetching <id>…`, rerenders detail and creates AbortSignal.timeout(15000). Success updates only that summary's count and notifies info `Refetched <id>: <count> models`; a structured error or thrown exception notifies error `Could not refetch <id>: <error>`. Finally it clears the boolean and status, and rerenders the detail only if selectedProviderId still equals the original id. Navigating away does not abort the operation. The 15-second signal is passed to onRefetch, but AUTH-032's local branch does not forward it, so this is not a universal deadline (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider-settings.ts:152-178). The dedicated test source covers refetch UI state and overlap suppression; it was read, not executed (ice:packages/coding-agent/test/ice-provider-settings.test.ts:1-90).
