Helpers create text/thinking/tool-call blocks, random tool ids unless supplied, and assistant messages with default api/provider faux, model faux-1, stopReason stop, zero usage, optional deferred/error/responseId, and timestamp option ?? Date.now(). createFauxCore defaults provider to faux and API to a fresh random id prefixed faux. An omitted OR empty model-definition array yields faux-1 / Faux Model, text+image input, reasoning:false, zero costs, context 128000, output 16384, baseUrl http://localhost:0. Custom definitions use id as missing name and the same per-field defaults. getModel() or a falsy id returns the first model; a truthy id requires exact equality (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:23-99; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:437-487; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:645-652).

setResponses shallow-copies a replacement queue, appendResponses appends, and pending count is queue length; these operations do not reset call counters, cache or deferred state. Each stream invocation synchronously shifts one step and increments callCount BEFORE queueMicrotask begins. Inside the microtask it first awaits onResponse({status:200, headers:{}}, requestModel), then checks for an empty queue/deferred submission/normal factory. A factory receives original context, stream options, mutable shared state and request model, and may return a promise. The returned message is structured-cloned, then api/provider/model are rewritten to core/request identity and usage recomputed. Empty queue yields an error-only stream `No more faux responses queued` with estimated usage; thrown/rejected factory or callback yields error-only with zero default usage. A preaborted signal does not prevent onResponse or normal factory evaluation; it is observed when streaming begins (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:107-154; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:282-291; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:489-563; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:654-672).

streamWithDeltas starts with content:[]/stopReason:pending. Default chunk sizes are3–5 tokens, each token represented by 4 JS UTF-16 code units. min is at least 1 and the minimum of configured/default min and max; max is at least min. Random size is inclusive of both endpoints, and empty text still emits one empty delta. Missing/nonpositive pacing schedules a microtask; positive pacing waits estimateTokens(chunk)/tokensPerSecond*1000. The core initializer assigning tokensPerSecond at line 446 is connector-redacted; scheduler semantics and the pacing test fixtures are visible, but the exact initializer is not asserted here (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:270-280; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:331-337; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:437-446; ice:packages/ai/test/faux-provider.test.ts:406-434; ice:packages/ai/test/faux-provider.test.ts:506-630).

field_changes.before:
TS tries a direct clipboard write before terminal escape output. Remote sessions can receive OSC 52 after a successful native write, while local success returns without issuing duplicate terminal clipboard writes.

copyToClipboard first calls addon.setText on platforms other than linux and catches failure. A successful local write returns. Remote means any truthy SSH_CONNECTION, SSH_CLIENT or MOSH_CONNECTION. If not yet copied, darwin executes pbcopy and win32 clip; otherwise it tries termux-clipboard-set when TERMUX_VERSION is truthy, then Wayland/X11. These synchronous command writes use input:text,5000 ms timeout and ignored stdout/stderr. X11 tries xclip -selection clipboard then xsel --clipboard --input (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:12-24; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:73-125).

Wayland is selected only with isWaylandSession and a truthy WAYLAND_DISPLAY. It first execs 'which wl-copy' without the 5000 ms options, then spawns wl-copy with piped stdin and ignored output. It ignores stdin EPIPE, writes/ends text, and resolves success only on close code0; error/null/nonzero counts failure. This asynchronous branch has no timeout. With DISPLAY present, failure falls back to X11; without Wayland selection, DISPLAY alone uses X11. Outer failures fall through (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:126-165).

When remote or still uncopied, emitOsc52 base64-encodes UTF-8 and refuses encoded length>100000. Otherwise it writes ESC]52;c;<base64>BEL to process.stdout and returns true without waiting for an acknowledgment or drain. copied becomes priorCopied||osc52Copied. If all attempts fail, throw 'Failed to copy to clipboard'. An oversized remote OSC payload does not turn a prior native success into failure. Tests specify local direct/shell success skipping OSC, remote ordering, fallback and size refusal; no copy was executed (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:26-32; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts:167-174; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/clipboard.test.ts:151-210).

field_changes.before:
TS normalizes line endings before locating a leading frontmatter block. It trims the body only when a closing fence was found, and malformed YAML propagates an error even when the caller only asked to strip metadata.

Normalize CRLF then bare CR to LF. The opener check is startsWith('---'), not a whole-line delimiter check. Find the first '\n---' starting at index3; absent opener/closer yields frontmatter:{} and the entire normalized, untrimmed body. With a closer, yamlString is slice(4, endIndex) and body is slice(endIndex+4).trim(), so characters following the three closing hyphens belong to body. Empty/falsy yamlString returns {}; otherwise yaml.parse is called and only null/undefined is converted to {}. The generic Record type is a cast: scalar/array values are returned as parsed. stripFrontmatter calls this parser and can therefore throw YAML errors (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/frontmatter.ts:8-39).

The direct suite specifies quoted keys/values, CRLF, invalid-YAML location text, literal block scalars ending in a newline, missing/unterminated fences, comment-only {} and untrimmed no-frontmatter bodies. These are inspected assertions only (ice:packages/coding-agent/test/frontmatter.test.ts:4-60).

Native normalizes the same newlines and largely copies the delimiter/slice contract using safe UTF-8 get ranges. parse_yaml returns an empty object for whitespace-only input but otherwise directly returns yaml_serde::from_str's Value. On a parse error it retries only after quoting unindented noncomment top-level scalar values containing ': ' unless they begin a quote/collection/block-scalar marker; it preserves the original error if that repair fails. This deliberate legacy repair is absent in TS (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/frontmatter.rs:22-89).

field_changes.before:
Export assembles local viewer assets and serialized session data into one HTML file. Live-session export can include the current system prompt, tool schemas and custom tool renderings; file-only export has no live runtime metadata.

exportSessionToHtml accepts ExportOptions or an output-path string. It requires a session file path and that path to exist, throwing distinct in-memory and nothing-to-export errors. It does not require a nonempty entry array after the file existence check. Data includes header, every getEntries entry, current leafId, optional state.systemPrompt, tools projected to name/description/parameters, and nonempty custom-renderer results. ExportFromFile resolves and checks its input, opens SessionManager and includes header/all entries/leaf only; it ignores an options.toolRenderer because it never invokes custom prerendering. SESSION-038 owns the input journal format and restoration interpretation (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts:236-306).

An explicit truthy output path is normalized with the shared path helper; otherwise the name is APP_NAME+'-session-'+basename(input,'.jsonl')+'.html' in the current working directory. Both APIs write synchronously as UTF-8, overwrite an existing destination and return the path. They do not create parent directories, stage an atomic replacement, or stream large sessions. Despite async declarations, local asset/file operations are synchronous. Read/write/serialization errors propagate (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts:272-315).

generateHtml synchronously reads template.html, template.css, template.js and the bundled Marked/Highlight.js files from getExportTemplateDir. It JSON-stringifies SessionData, UTF-8/base64 encodes it and places that payload in the session-data element, preventing raw session text from terminating the script/data element. CSS placeholders are replaced in THEME_VARS/BODY_BG/CONTAINER_BG/INFO_BG order, then HTML placeholders in CSS/JS/SESSION_DATA/MARKED_JS/HIGHLIGHT_JS order. Each call is a single String.replace using replacement-string semantics, not a function replacement or global template engine. Browser assets are local inline content; no network asset fetch is necessary merely to open the artifact (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts:130-175; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.html:1-56).

Theme variables enumerate every resolved color. Explicit export page/card/info colors use nullish precedence over derived colors. The fallback source color is userMessageBg or #343541; derivation parses six-digit hex or rgb integer syntax, uses gamma-adjusted luminance with threshold 0.5, then selects light page brightness0.96/card original/info offsets +10,+5,-20, or dark page0.7/card0.85/info +20,+15,+0. Components are clamped/rounded by the brightness/offset helpers, but rgb parser input itself is not range-validated. Unparseable input uses the source's fixed RGB fallbacks. TUI-004 owns palette resolution; this entry owns the additional export color derivation and template insertion (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts:18-127).

The CSS supplies a 12 px/18px monospace viewer, a default 400 px sidebar bounded240–840 px, an 800 px main column, a 900 px mobile layout boundary, print adjustments and exact preformatted output/ANSI-line whitespace rules. Bundled vendor headers identify Marked18.0.5/MIT and Highlight.js11.9.0/BSD-3-Clause; they are frozen source snapshots, not externally verified release downloads. Marked lines38/43 were connector-redacted and remain unverified; every other vendor line and all exporter assets were read. No browser export was run.

field_changes.before:
The viewer reconstructs a navigable tree from the embedded entries and shows one root-to-leaf conversation path. Its browser controls operate entirely on that data, with optional metadata supplied by a containing share viewer.

Startup decodes base64 through atob→Uint8Array→TextDecoder→JSON.parse with no local catch/schema check. ice-url-params meta content takes precedence over location.search; a truthy leafId parameter wins over the embedded leaf, and targetId controls highlighting/scrolling. Entry and tool-call maps keep the last value for duplicate IDs. Label entries update labels only when both targetId and label are truthy, so a later empty label does not remove an earlier label. Null/undefined/self-parent and orphan entries become roots; children sort by numeric timestamps, roots retain source order. Parent traversal stops for missing/falsy/self parent but has no visited-ID guard, so a multi-node cycle can hang traversal. A robust native export boundary should reject or handle malformed trees instead of copying that weakness (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:8-145).

Clicking a node chooses a descendant by repeatedly following the last timestamp-sorted child; this is a local newest-child walk, not a global maximum timestamp over all leaves. Flattening prefers the active branch and recomputes indentation/connectors after filtering by attaching descendants to the nearest visible ancestor. Filters are default, no-tools, user-only, labeled-only and all. The current leaf is returned before every hide/filter/search check. Other assistant entries without nonblank text are hidden unless stopReason is truthy and neither stop nor toolUse; thus the condition also treats length as exceptional. Default excludes label/custom/model_change/thinking_level_change, no-tools also excludes toolResult, user-only requires a user message, and labeled-only requires a defined label. Search checks that every token appears in lowercased searchable text assembled from labels/roles/content and selected metadata; compaction contributes its type keyword, not the summary body. The search-token initializer at line 369 is connector-redacted, so its exact preprocessing is explicitly unverified (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:155-363; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:374-558).

Initial tree rendering constructs DOM rows/listeners; later navigation updates active classes/path markers without rebuilding the complete filtered order. Search/filter controls force a rebuild. Per-entry content DOM is cached, then cloned on navigation, so expanded/collapsed state is not persistent across branch replacement. Navigation recomputes the global header and selected path, routes a tool-result target to its call element, highlights for 2000 ms and scrolls after a zero-delay timeout. Global stats still describe all embedded entries, not just that selected branch. Invalid truthy leaf IDs can yield an empty path rather than falling back to a valid leaf (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:708-799; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1461-1551; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1853-1865).

Download reconstructs an optional header using {type:'header',...header}, followed by all entries, joins with LF without a terminal LF, creates an application/x-ndjson Blob, downloads as header.id or session plus .jsonl, then revokes the object URL. Because the spread follows type, an existing header.type wins. Deep links include leafId and targetId; an injected ice-share-base-url is concatenated with '&'+params, otherwise the current URL keeps its hash and first empty-valued query key as the gist ID. The template does not read ICE_SHARE_VIEWER_URL or upload a gist; that is a separate TUI share-command boundary. Browser copy tries navigator.clipboard.writeText then hidden-textarea execCommand('copy'), gives a 1500 ms success indicator, and can leave the textarea if the fallback throws before removal (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1069-1171).

Sidebar width persists under localStorage key ice-share:v1:sidebar-width. It starts from CSS defaults400/min240/max840 (JS fallback max720), reserves320px content space, clamps on resize, supports pointer drag and double-click reset, and uses a 900 px mobile query with an overlay toggle. T toggles currently rendered thinking and O tool outputs, except in editable/button targets. Escape clears search and navigates to the original leaf before the editable-element guard; it does not force a full tree rebuild in that path. Toggle booleans are not reapplied automatically to newly cloned branch content. The HTML contains image-modal markup, but this source has no corresponding image-modal activation handler; do not claim implemented image zoom (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1644-1865).

createToolHtmlRenderer receives a definition lookup, theme, cwd and width default 100. It owns separate maps for prior call components, prior result components, arbitrary state objects and arguments. renderCall caches arguments before looking up the definition, invokes renderCall with the previous call component, stores the returned component, renders at width and converts its lines. Context has toolCallId, args, cwd, shared state, lastComponent, invalidate no-op, executionStarted=true, argsComplete=true, showImages=false; call context is expanded=false, isPartial=true, isError=false. Missing definitions/renderers or any thrown error return undefined so the exporter can fall back (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/tool-renderer.ts:58-119).

renderResult passes content/details/isError as a generic tool result, renders collapsed first with isPartial=false, stores that component, then renders expanded with the just-stored collapsed component as lastComponent and the same per-call state. Both variants remove leading/trailing lines that become blank after stripping only ESC[digits/semicolons m SGR sequences and trimming. Return always includes expanded, even empty; collapsed is included only when nonempty and different. Any error in either phase returns undefined for the entire result, including a successful collapsed phase. Maps have no size bound or explicit dispose and live as long as this renderer object (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/tool-renderer.ts:44-55; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/tool-renderer.ts:121-173).

The export traversal preserves entry order. For assistant tool calls outside bash/read/write/edit/ls, a truthy call rendering creates/replaces the record for its ID. For tool results, it invokes result rendering when a prior record exists or the result's name is not one of those template-rendered tools; a truthy result object merges collapsed/expanded strings with existing call HTML. A later call with the same ID can overwrite earlier result data. The arbitrary ToolHtmlRenderer interface itself may throw and is not caught by preRenderCustomTools; only the standard created renderer has catch/fallback behavior (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/index.ts:177-230).

field_changes.before:
The client sends management requests to a normalized router base URL and combines server events with repeated catalog reads. Each ordinary HTTP request has a timeout, but the overall load/download/unload waits have no independent deadline.

URL normalization trims input, requires http or https, clears query/fragment, strips trailing path slashes and one terminal /v1, and removes the final slash from the serialized URL. It does not require loopback, reject URL userinfo or restrict a path prefix. llamaInferenceUrl appends /v1. request preserves supplied headers, adds application/json when body is defined, adds Bearer auth only for a truthy key and combines a 15000 ms AbortSignal.timeout with any caller signal. It attempts response.json even for failures; invalid JSON becomes undefined. Non-OK throws a nested error.message when it is a nonempty string, otherwise an HTTP-status fallback. No retry, redirect override or response byte bound is implemented (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:141-180).

GET /models optionally adds ?reload=1. The response requires data array and every member to have string id and string status.value; it does not validate status against the declared unloaded/loading/loaded/downloading/sleeping union or validate nested metadata. Load posts {model} to /models/load, unload to /models/unload, download to /models. unloadAndWait first unloads, then lists until the model is absent or exactly unloaded, sleeping100 ms between reads. Request timeouts repeat per request and therefore do not bound the whole loop (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:182-211).

watch GETs /models/sse with optional Bearer and only its caller signal, requiring OK/body but no MIME check. It uses a nonfatal streaming TextDecoder, normalizes CRLF within each decoded chunk, splits LF-LF frames, collects only lines starting data:, trims their leading payload whitespace and joins them with LF. JSON events require string model/event. Malformed JSON and exceptions thrown by onEvent are swallowed by the same catch. There is no buffer/frame/record limit, decoder EOF flush, residual-frame processing, reader.cancel or releaseLock finally. Chunk-local CRLF normalization can miss a CR/LF split across chunks. These source weaknesses are not required properties of a native client (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:213-245).

loadAndWait starts a fire-and-forget watcher before the POST and suppresses watcher rejection. It accepts only target-model model_status/status_change events; loaded sets an eventLoaded flag and unloaded records a load error. After POST and initial progress it polls: caller abort first, catalog loaded success, then eventLoaded with missing catalog entry yields a synthetic loaded record, then failed-status/event error, then250 ms sleep. Thus catalog loaded wins even if a failure flag was also observed. A defined exit_code selects the exit-code error message. Finally it unlinks and aborts the watcher without awaiting watcher completion. Load progress recognizes current then stage strings, replaces underscores in stage labels, clamps a numeric stage fraction to 0..1 and computes (stageIndex+fraction)/stageCount when possible; it does not explicitly reject NaN (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:86-106; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:247-286).

downloadAndWait similarly starts a watcher, tracks download_finished/download_failed/download_progress, posts the request and polls with 500 ms sleeps. Each loop checks caller abort, then an event failure, then catalog. A downloading entry sets sawDownloading and updates progress; otherwise finished or an existing entry after sawDownloading or at least 2 polls returns a final reload list. Merely seeing a non-downloading entry twice can therefore count as completion without an explicit finished event. Progress sums numeric done/total from nested progress or the supplied object, ignores nonnumeric pairs, rejects only total<=0 and reports an unclamped done/total ratio; negative/nonfinite inputs are not otherwise validated. formatBytes uses raw B below 1024, then KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB with one decimal for values>=10 and two otherwise. Finally abort/unlink does not await watch termination (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:108-139; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/client.ts:288-331).

The full llama suite checks URL normalization, model mapping/auth/cache and fixture-driven SSE load/download progress. It does not prove real server compatibility, stalled-loop termination, arbitrary chunk boundaries or UI rollback; no server or test was executed.

Search GETs /api/models with search=query, filter=gguf, sort=downloads, direction=-1, limit=20. It requires an array, filters out nonobject/nonstring-id entries, preserves returned order and gives downloads 0 unless the field is typeof number; finiteness/integer validation is absent. Details encodes each slash-separated ID segment and GETs /api/models/{id}?blobs=true. It requires an object, walks array siblings, accepts case-insensitive .gguf paths, extracts basename and excludes names beginning mmproj case-insensitively (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/huggingface.ts:100-133).

Grouping removes one terminal -ddddd-of-ddddd shard suffix, recognizes the source suffix grammar for optional UD- plus IQ/Q digit-and-underscore forms, BF16/F16/F32 or MXFP digit forms, and uppercases the quantization. It sums every numeric size for that group; any member missing numeric size makes the reported total undefined. It does not validate shard completeness, uniqueness, positive/finite byte counts or a complete numbered sequence. Q4_K_M sorts first, then known size ascending with unknown at Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, then locale name. field_changes.before:
The /llama command opens a dedicated TUI workflow and ignores its command arguments. It coordinates router operations and user decisions; it is not a parser for load/unload/download/login subcommands.

Outside ctx.mode==='tui' the command warns and returns. It obtains generic provider auth, warns to use /login llama.cpp if absent, and constructs the router client from result.env.LLAMA_BASE_URL or auth.baseUrl. The first catalog read and every post-action read run through syncCatalog. On read failure, a Retry/Close selector loops only the read; it does not replay a failed mutation. Connection errors are Error instances whose lowercased name/message contain 'fetch failed','timeout' or 'network'. Nonconnection action errors are shown only after a successful reread, while connection-classified action errors are suppressed there. There is no additional ICE_OFFLINE check in this command flow (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:7-40; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:181-227).

The model list sorts exactly loaded first then ID locale order, displays at most 12 rows and appends the internal '\0download' action. Sleeping models are described and acted on as loaded, but do not receive the list's loaded-sort preference. Context labels use n_ctx??n_ctx_train when truthy, otherwise the first positive finite argument after --ctx-size/-c/-ctx. Confirmed unload awaits unloadAndWait then catalog sync. Loading while other loaded/sleeping models exist asks Unload all and load/Keep loaded and load/Cancel. Replace mode sequentially unloads old models before entering the target-load try block; a failure during that pre-try unload loop can leave earlier models unloaded without restoration. Within the later try/catch, cancelled or failed target load best-effort restores old models sequentially and refreshes; restoration failure preserves the original load error in catch. Cancel sends unload(target), not unloadAndWait (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:64-133; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:23-51; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:321-388).

Download finds a client HF token, opens search, parses a colon only after the first slash, fetches details and shows auto/manual gated-access guidance with Continue/Back. It explicitly tells the user the llama server needs its own authorized HF_TOKEN; the client token is not sent as a router credential. When no quantization was supplied, available options include sizes and Q4_K_M 'recommended'; an already supplied quantization is not checked against the discovered list. It asks the router to download repository[:quant], supports unload-as-cancel, then syncs the returned catalog. Detail fetch itself is not tied to a view-level cancellation signal (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:135-179).

Search trims input, requires 2 characters for a new query, debounces500 ms and aborts the previous request. A per-view map caches by lowercase query without TTL/size bound. Responses enter the cache before checking closed/aborted/current-query state, so a stale response can populate cache while leaving the visible state untouched. Fuzzy filtering uses TUI-235 for membership but preserves original API order. Selection clamps after filtering and wraps on up/down; at most 10 centered rows show. Confirm prefers a query matching the exact owner/repository[:quant] regex over the highlighted result, and cancel closes once while clearing debounce/aborting request (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:96-274).

runWithProgress starts the operation immediately and converts success/failure into a fulfilled settlement object. It races that against the progress cancel key, then asks confirmation. A declined confirmation or already completed operation resumes/finishes normally. On confirmed stop it awaits the cancel callback first and aborts the operation controller in finally, then awaits settled and returns cancelled. If cancel itself rejects, control skips the later await/return and propagates that error; the operation's wrapped settlement remains observed. The 40-character bar clamps filled length but prints the raw rounded percentage, with no finite-number guard. showLlamaUi routes run completion to done and errors to notify then done; view content replacement clears the old progress resolver without settling an abandoned progress promise (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:305-319; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:419-543).

The doc's router setup flags, filesystem examples and server token guidance were read as documentation only. Existing llama tests exercise provider/client fixtures, not this complete UI recovery/cancellation flow. No model server, download, token file or test was invoked.

field_changes.before:
Preview text is provisional until the final turn is validated. The adapter reconciles that preview only with the first final text block, then emits any remaining blocks in their original order.

stream immediately returns an AssistantMessageEventStream and starts run asynchronously. Its output message starts with role assistant, requested model/API/provider, empty content, zero usage/cost, stopReason stop, a wall-clock timestamp and a diagnostic {type:'claude-agent-sdk', timestamp, details:{billing:'external', identityRewriting:false}}. start is pushed only after request validation/serialization and before the step fetch, so early rejected options can produce error without start (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:226-251; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:327-338).

After ready, each text_delta requires a string and appends to previewText. Buffer.byteLength(previewText)>2*1024*1024 fails. The first preview delta, including an empty string, creates text block0 and emits text_start at index0. Every delta replaces output.content with the accumulated first text block and emits text_delta with that index. These are mutable partial-output references in the TS adapter, not independently cloned snapshots. A later validation failure can leave previously delivered preview text visible; no rollback event is issued. Tool-call events have not yet been emitted at this stage (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:363-373).

After the entire terminal passes MISC-035 validation, a started preview requires blocks[0] to be text and its final text to start with the exact preview string. A preview is never retroactively assigned to a later text block after thinking or a tool call. output.content is set to the complete first text block; any missing suffix is emitted as one text_delta using the UTF-16 prefix length, followed by text_end. Since the prefix comparison is exact, that suffix boundary follows the original preview string. Remaining blocks begin at index1, preserving mixed text/thinking/text order (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:399-414).

Without a preview, or for later blocks, each text block emits start/delta/end, thinking emits thinking_start/thinking_delta/thinking_end, and a toolCall emits toolcall_start then toolcall_end without an intermediate argument-delta event. The block is appended before its event sequence, so contentIndex is the current output length before append. Finally done carries the validated stop reason and full message. The mixed-block hardening test clones events and expects text indices0 and 2 with thinking at 1; another rejects a preview whose text belongs only to a later block. Streaming tests hold the final record back, confirm early text and no duplicate suffix, and ensure an inconsistent preview emits no toolcall_end. These were read, not run.

field_changes.before:
Each request owns an abort controller and a fixed cleanup path. Failures discard its local handle and produce one terminal error, while best-effort bridge cancellation remains distinct from proof that external work stopped.

The timer starts near the beginning of run with Math.min(options.timeoutMs ?? 600000,600000); there is no explicit lower-bound, integer or finiteness validation of timeoutMs. The caller's abort event triggers the same controller, and a pre-aborted signal is checked before active-key acquisition or network inference. The controller signal is passed to step fetch, but token reads, onPayload/onResponse and reader cleanup are not independently raced against a deadline. Consequently the timer requests cancellation rather than guaranteeing every await and external operation finishes within 600000 ms (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:252-276; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:328-342).

cancelHandle sends POST /api/services/claude-sdk/cancel with Bearer token, JSON {version:1, sessionId:wireSessionId, handle}, redirect:error and AbortSignal.timeout(2000). It uses global fetch rather than the custom inference fetch. It ignores HTTP status/body and suppresses fetch failures; success is not an acknowledgement that SDK work or descendants have ended. The comment names server TTL and disconnected-request deadline as final guards, but those are external server assumptions, not verified client guarantees. close snapshots current handles, clears the map, tries to reread a token, and concurrently cancels all captured states. Token failure returns after the map is already cleared. close does not abort/join active request controllers; an in-flight ready event can repopulate the map after the snapshot. session_shutdown awaiting close therefore does not by itself establish an empty/finished active set (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:182-205; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/extension.ts:33-35).

On failure, only the request that acquired its key deletes that handle and cancels selected state. If token acquisition failed before selected was populated, an existing cached key is deleted without a cancellation handle. The output stopReason is aborted only when the local controller is aborted, otherwise error. Local abort uses the fixed cancelled-or-timed-out message. SafeBridgeFailure exposes only predefined safe text; other exceptions become a generic transport/validation message. Remote error.message is ignored. The code table covers subscription_required, unauthorized, session_lost, session_conflict, tool_protocol, capacity, unsupported, timeout and upstream; unknown codes use upstream. A server timeout code can therefore yield reason error when the local controller did not abort. There is no provider/API fallback or automatic replay after session loss (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:152-165; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:374-377; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:431-442).

Finally the timer/listener are removed, the owning active key is released, temporary selected handles are deleted/cancelled and stream.end is called. A temporary failed request with selected state can call cancel once in catch and again in finally; each is best-effort and separately has a 2000 ms signal. The pre-abort test expects zero inference calls. The server-error test's fixture and one assertion contain connector-redacted text at lines88/90, so those lines are excluded; visible assertions and implementation establish the fixed code-message/fallback policy without reconstructing the hidden literal. No bridge, login, SDK process or cancellation was executed.

field_changes.before:
The runner gives explicit CLI provider/model values precedence over environment defaults and forwards other arguments to Vitest. A harness may override that default with its own model. The runner and harness validate selection at different points, so launching without a default is allowed only when the executed harnesses supply their own models.

The root npm eval script forwards to the private @zykairotis/ice-evals workspace. run-evals.mjs accepts --provider value, --model value and their = forms; repeated values overwrite earlier values. Separate-form values must be nonempty and must not start with '-'. After trimming, the presence of either CLI selector requires both CLI values; a missing CLI half is not filled from the environment. Without any CLI selector, trimmed ICE_PROVIDER and ICE_MODEL must either both exist or both be absent. All other arguments are retained in encounter order. field_changes.before:
Every run uses a fresh session and workspace while retaining the application's normal model authentication path. Optional prompt transformation sees the complete initial system prompt and is applied through a resource reload. Prompt and reload steps then execute sequentially, and the output callback sees the live final session before cleanup.

The timer and initial abort check precede model selection. ModelRuntime.create() is called with its normal defaults before the temporary root exists; getModel(provider, id) must return a model or the run rejects with 'Eval model not found: provider/id'. Only then does mkdtemp create an ice-eval- directory under the OS temp directory. workspace and agent children are created in parallel. createAgentSessionServices receives cwd, agentDir, that model runtime and SettingsManager.inMemory(); it does not replace normal model credentials with a temporary credential store. A resourceLoader systemPromptOverride closure is installed only when a transform was supplied. SessionManager.create uses the workspace and a sibling sessions directory, and its session ID is immediately placed in the 'runId' artifact. createAgentSessionFromServices selects the resolved model, thinkingLevel='off', and forwards noTools without changing its schema (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:115-151).

The transform callback is synchronous and receives evalSession.systemPrompt. Its returned string must have a nonempty trim; the original returned string, including intentional whitespace, remains the override. evalSession.reload() applies it. The harness then rejects any nonempty initial extension-path list, which asserts starting isolation before the test can create resources. It does not assert that the entire environment or model credential state is empty (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:153-168).

A string input becomes one prompt step; array steps retain order. Prompt steps call the stricter completion adapter in MISC-043. Every other branch in the typed prompt/reload union invokes reload; there is no additional runtime discriminator validation in this loop. Reloads may occur before the first prompt or after the last prompt, but at least one prompt must set response. The final response is the last prompt's returned text, even if a later reload changes session resources. When options contains an output property, its callback is awaited with {response,session}; otherwise the string is returned. The adapter's generic restricts custom output to JsonValue, while actual external createHarness normalization is a dependency boundary rather than locally implemented JSON validation (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:169-180; ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:246-259).

field_changes.before:
The table generates baseline-then-candidate rows for each repetition. Inputs are paired by a trimmed explicit string ID when available, otherwise by a hash of strict canonical JSON. Iteration metadata is attached before execution and merged into successful or externally attached partial runs.

Options accept either candidate or candidates with a baseline and optional repetitions. The implementation chooses the singular property when 'candidate' in options, otherwise uses the candidate array. Default repetitions is 1. validateOptions rejects a whitespace-only evalSet, zero candidates, duplicate exact harness.name values and repetitions that are not a positive safe integer. It does not trim stored evalSet/names or independently reject an empty harness name. Rows enumerate repetitions1..N, with baseline first then candidates in declaration order. The builder does not randomize or schedule execution; callers use describe.for and may independently configure Vitest sequencing (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:114-128; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:157-193).

deriveInputKey first checks non-null, non-array object inputs with an 'id' property, including an inherited property. A nonempty trimmed string ID is returned directly and bypasses validation of all other input fields. Otherwise canonicalizeJson accepts null/string/boolean and finite numbers, dense arrays with an own property at every numeric index, and only Object.prototype/null-prototype objects. It rejects other primitive types, non-finite numbers, sparse arrays, cycles and non-plain object prototypes. Object.entries selects enumerable own string-keyed fields, sorts keys lexically with < and >, recursively canonicalizes values and reconstructs an object before JSON.stringify. The lexical comparison is JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit order. Because the sorted entries are reconstructed as an ordinary object, canonical array-index keys from '0' through '4294967294' serialize first in numeric order, followed by the other sorted string keys; the final JSON text is not a generic all-keys-lexicographic encoding. The hash also inherits JSON.stringify number/string encoding, including -0 becoming 0. The WeakSet tracks ancestors and deletes on return, so repeated noncyclic object references are allowed. SHA-256 of that canonical JSON string becomes a lower-case hex input key. The final group key is JSON.stringify([inputKey, repetition]); explicit IDs and hash keys share the same string namespace (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:66-112).

Each wrapper sets artifact 'vitestEvalsHarnessIteration' before calling the underlying harness. The artifact is {schemaVersion:1, evalSet, groupKey, harness, baseline, candidates, repetition}. On success, it mutates run.artifacts by merging context.artifacts, then existing run.artifacts, then the authoritative iteration value. On failure it asks external getHarnessRunFromError for a partial run; when present it performs the same merge and rethrows through attachHarnessRunToError. Errors without an attached run are rethrown unchanged. A group-key error happens before the artifact is set (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:130-155).

The parser is intentionally less strict than the table builder: it requires a non-array object, schemaVersion===1, the named string fields, an array of string candidate names and typeof repetition==='number'. It does not require finite/positive/integer repetition, nonempty strings, unique candidates or baseline/harness membership. The direct tests cover canonical key order, trimmed IDs, array order, unsupported/sparse/cyclic inputs, row order, singular candidate and success metadata. They do not assert all builder/parser validation branches or the partial-error attachment path.

field_changes.before:
The summary uses matched observations for the same file, test name, input key and repetition. Correctness is the difference in pass rates, while tokens, latency and estimated cost are separate paired metrics. Missing scores or telemetry remain unavailable and contribute explicit coverage or diagnostics.

groupObservations groups first by evalSet. The first observation fixes that set's baseline; later conflicting baseline declarations are not validated. Candidate names are unioned, retaining their smallest observed declaration index. Each group key is JSON.stringify([file,testName,groupKey]); the stored repetition and other group labels come from the first observation, so repetition only affects grouping independently when already encoded by the table's groupKey. Runs with the same file, leaf test.name and input key can collide even if their fullName differs. Observations are stored as arrays per harness, retaining duplicates. Candidates sort by retained index then localeCompare name; eval sets sort by localeCompare, groups by groupKey then repetition (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:112-161).

Every group and declared harness is diagnosed once with this precedence: zero observations→missing-observation; more than one→duplicate-observation; one errored→harness-error; one unscored→missing-score; one other non-scored outcome→unscorable-outcome. Diagnostics are shared across all candidate comparisons and finally sort by evalSet, file, groupKey, repetition, harness; they are not duplicated for each pair. Each candidate is paired only with the declared baseline, and only groups with exactly one observation for each side become candidate pairs. totalPairs is all groups in the eval set, including groups with missing or duplicate data (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:164-210; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:284-328).

Correctness includes a pair only when both outcomes are scored. A score>=1 is a pass; no rounding, clamping or fractional-credit pass threshold is substituted. Baseline/candidate wins mean only one side passes; ties mean both pass or both fail. Pass rates divide by eligiblePairs; zero eligible pairs yields null rates and lift. Lift is candidateRate-baselineRate, rounded through Number(difference.toPrecision(15)). The public summary function itself does not revalidate score finiteness; its normal reporter caller filters scores under MISC-046. Metrics likewise require two scored observations and two defined finite values, independently for totalTokens, totalMs, estimatedCostUsd. Negative finite values are not rejected by this helper. It computes each side's mean over that metric's eligible pairs and the same 15-significant-digit candidate-minus-baseline difference. No value is imputed for missing telemetry, and no confidence interval or significance test is computed (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:104-110; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:212-281).

Formatting returns empty when every eval set has no comparisons, even if a manually supplied report has diagnostics. Otherwise it prints 'Eval Comparisons', set names, right-aligned9-character labels, baseline and candidate names and correctness eligible/total pair counts. Pass rates use one decimal percent and lift uses signed one-decimal percentage points. Tokens and milliseconds use one decimal; estimated USD uses four. Positive correctness is green, negative correctness red; lower efficiency metrics are green, higher red; zero deltas gray and unavailable values yellow. Metric coverage is appended only for a nonzero eligible count that differs from correctness eligiblePairs; a wholly unavailable metric has no separate zero-pair suffix. Incomplete observations follow with reason, file/testName, repetition, harness. Styling uses Node styleText; terminal color emission policy is not reimplemented locally (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:330-438).

The full direct suite covers correctness versus efficiency, missing observations/telemetry, file separation, harness-error and unscored exclusion, baseline-only candidate comparisons, declared missing harnesses, deduplicated diagnostics and terminal strings. These assertions were inspected only; no model/test execution or statistical result was produced.

field_changes.before:
The smoke suite checks one no-tools answer and basic model telemetry. The extension suite compares two system-prompt variants on the same two-prompt workflow with an intervening resource reload. Its judge records task correctness, while hard assertions protect the intended prompt-treatment setup.

The smoke harness uses noTools='all' and the default harness/model selection. It asks for the capital of France, requires output.trim()==='Paris', result.errors===[], usage.provider/model equal the ICE_PROVIDER/ICE_MODEL environment values and totalTokens>0. It supplies no iteration table or judge, so the local comparison collector ignores it, though its recognized harness run can still be indexed. The runner may launch with no model defaults, but executing this shipped default-model smoke test still fails selection unless defaults exist; the no-default allowance applies when selected harnesses configure their own model (ice:packages/evals/src/smoke.eval.ts:1-18; ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:49-63).

createExtensionAuthoringHarness projects the response, markers for Guidelines and ICE documentation in the effective system prompt, resource-loader errors, each loaded extension path/tool-name list and the UTF-8 source at <session cwd>/.ice/extensions/hello.ts when it exists. The baseline 'system-prompt-without-docs' truncates the default prompt at the first '\nGuidelines:\n' and throws if absent. Candidate 'default-system-prompt' removes the last '\nCurrent working directory: ' suffix and throws if absent. The two transforms are not arbitrary whole-section parsers; they use these exact string markers and slices. evalHarnessTable uses its default one repetition with baseline then candidate (ice:packages/evals/src/extensions.eval.ts:18-51; ice:packages/evals/src/extensions.eval.ts:100-103).

Both runs ask the model to create a hello tool accepting a name, reload the session, then ask it to call the tool for Bob and respond with exactly the greeting. The source path is a fixed expected hello.ts even though the first prompt does not explicitly name that file. The judge fails when that source is unavailable. It extracts imports with a regex matching from/import followed by whitespace and a quoted specifier; this is not a TypeScript parser and does not inspect dynamic import(...) forms. It requires a canonical @zykairotis/ice-coding-agent import, rejects matched @mariozechner/* or @sinclair/typebox* imports, requires zero loader errors and a loaded 'hello' tool, and requires a normalized successful call named hello with arguments.name==='Bob' and result==='Hello, Bob!'. Final response must equal 'Hello, Bob!' exactly without trimming. All conditions must pass for score1; otherwise score0 with semicolon-joined rationale metadata (ice:packages/evals/src/extensions.eval.ts:53-98).

describeEval receives that judge and judgeThreshold:null, expressing observational scoring rather than a score threshold gate. The test records hello.ts as a text/typescript UTF-8 source artifact when source exists, requiring a string runId first. It then hard-asserts that Guidelines/documentation markers match whether the harness name is 'default-system-prompt'. The README directs comparative suites to use judges for correctness and hard assertions only for setup/infrastructure invariants; it states that expect.soft still fails a test. That external framework behavior is not independently executed here. Four local unit suites test helper contracts, while the two *.eval.ts files are model-backed scenarios whose outcomes remain unverified.
